title: A borehole and hand pump for forty households in Karaba
story: The nearest working water point is an hour's walk each way and it runs dry from March. Forty households in Karaba share it, and the walk falls on the girls in the family, which is why half of them stop attending school in the dry season. We are raising 14,000 USD for a borehole, a hand pump and a concrete apron, drilled by a contractor who has sunk four wells in the district. When the work is signed off the water point passes to a village committee of six, three of them women, elected before the drilling starts.
reviewerNote: Approved under fi sabilillah, and this one went to our advisor before I recorded anything. Two questions were live and they are not the same question: whether a shared water point falls inside that heading under our policy, and who owns the asset once it is finished, which is where recognised positions genuinely differ on a project campaign. I asked the organizer and was told the completed water point passes to an elected village committee, and the committee's constitution was sent through. That answer decided the route rather than the outcome. Our policy requires funds under the poor and needy headings to reach an individual as cash or goods, and an asset held by a committee does not do that, so I have left those two lines unresolved instead of recording support I cannot evidence; what would resolve them is a mechanism vesting ownership in named individuals, which this campaign does not have and was not asked to invent. The forty households were separately evidenced as below the threshold our policy uses, which is context for the reading I applied and not a basis of its own, since nothing reaches them as cash or goods. Our policy does verify water supply for a poor community under the contemporary reading of fi sabilillah, and the scoped question I put to the advisor was whether a project of this shape falls inside it with ownership documented as it is. The answer was that it does, and that is the basis on the file. I am not recording a view on the wider disagreement about ownership transfer, so the next reviewer sees the route I took and the reason for it rather than a conclusion I did not reach.
